items.text: The overview API endpoint already provides the full dependency graph (edges as [from,to] pairs, unblocked/blocked lists, all items, all initiatives with rollup). The depgraph package supports topological sort, cycle detection, and dependents lookup. This covers ~70% of what the Topology lens needs. Missing: capture nodes, scenario-targeting edges (from acceptance_allow globs), and execution/run edges for Flow and Operations lenses.

Execution records already have parent_execution_id for follow-up chains, backlog_kind+backlog_name for executes edges, and run_id for spawned_run edges. The execution list endpoint supports filtering by status, mode, backlog reference, and date range. This is sufficient for the Flow lens without new API development — just a graph-shaped projection of existing data.

The prompt-manager graph has 18 files (~2400 lines) using React Flow v12 + Dagre. Key patterns to adopt independently: Zustand store with highlight/dim/hide query modes, BFS neighborhood selection (type-constrained), desktop popover + mobile bottom sheet for inspector, onlyRenderVisibleElements + lightweight edges above 300-edge threshold, MiniMap with 120-node threshold, auto-fit via change-signature detection, three layout modes (hierarchical/compact/grouped).

The current UI has 6 Zustand stores (backlog, backlogForm, scenarios, execution, agentRuns, captures), 7 API services, and 30+ domain types. All stores use localStorage persistence with configurable max items (100-200). The existing store pattern is well-established and the graph store should follow the same conventions (Zustand + localStorage for viewport/settings, selectors with useShallow).

items.topic: Inspector action model per node type
items.context: When a user clicks a node in the graph, the inspector panel opens. We need to define what information and actions each node type exposes. This directly determines whether the graph workspace is operationally useful or just a visualization.

options.label: Rich contextual actions: full detail view + lens-specific actions in inspector
options.rationale: Each node type shows its full detail card (same content as the current detail pages) plus contextual actions relevant to the active lens. E.g., a BacklogItem in Topology shows metadata + deps + workshop state; in Flow shows execution history + queue/run actions; in Operations shows live status + stop/restart. Advantage: the inspector replaces the need to navigate away. Risk: complex to build, may duplicate detail page logic.

options.label: Summary + navigate: inspector shows summary card with 'Open details' link
options.rationale: Inspector shows a compact summary (title, status, key stats) and a prominent link to the existing detail page. Simpler to build, avoids duplicating detail page logic. Risk: more navigation clicks, graph feels like a visualization layer rather than a workspace.

items.topic: Graph data API: extend overview or dedicated endpoint
items.context: The overview endpoint returns items, initiatives, dep graph, and summary stats. The graph needs additional data: captures, execution records, agent runs, scenario-targeting edges, and lens-specific filtering. We need to decide the API shape.

options.label: Dedicated /api/v1/graph endpoint with lens parameter
options.rationale: A new endpoint that accepts ?lens=topology|flow|operations and returns only the nodes and edges relevant to that lens. Clean separation from overview. Can optimize per-lens queries independently. Backend builds the full node/edge graph server-side and filters by lens.

options.label: Extend overview to include all graph data, filter client-side
options.rationale: Add captures, executions, runs, and all edge types to the overview response. Client filters by lens. Simpler backend (one endpoint), but response payload grows large and forces the client to receive data it may not need.

options.label: Composite: overview for Topology, separate endpoints for Flow and Operations
options.rationale: Reuse overview for the Topology lens (it already has most of what's needed). Add /api/v1/graph/flow and /api/v1/graph/operations for the other lenses. Avoids touching existing endpoint but creates API fragmentation.

items.topic: Anti-chaos guardrails: default filters and node caps
items.context: Without guardrails, a graph with hundreds of backlog items, executions, and captures becomes unusable. We need default filtering and clustering rules to keep the graph comprehensible at any scale.

options.label: Initiative-based clustering with status filters
options.rationale: Default: group nodes by initiative (collapsed clusters showing rollup counts), hide completed/archived items, cap visible unclustered nodes at ~50. User can expand clusters to see individual items. Each lens has its own default status filter (e.g., Topology hides archived, Flow shows only active pipeline, Operations shows only running). Advantage: scales naturally with initiative adoption. Risk: items without an initiative need a fallback group.

options.label: Priority-based filtering with progressive disclosure
options.rationale: Default: show only priority 1-3 items. User can lower the threshold to reveal more. No clustering — relies on filtering to control density. Simpler to implement but doesn't leverage the initiative grouping that already exists.

options.label: Time-window filtering: show only recent + active items
options.rationale: Default: show items created/updated within the last N days plus anything in active status. Older completed items are hidden. Works for any scale but loses the relationship context of older-but-connected items.

plan_updates: Incorporated 3 settled decisions from round 1 (independent graph, all 3 lenses, activity-first sidebar). Added 4 new findings: overview API data shape, execution record edges for Flow lens, PM graph patterns catalog, existing store conventions. Defined lens-specific node/edge visibility rules in Finding 5. Updated Limitations with 3 new open items (inspector actions, API shape, anti-chaos). Summary section now written.
